If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to correct downward bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.33) in the last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to late horizon (16–30 days) to dampen volatility overreaction.  
When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, cap the slope at 0.5% per day to prevent runaway growth.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to prevent premature bottoming.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is below 70% of recent high, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon to capture momentum.
